model_paper.paper_title: Chapter 3 Model Assessment - Empires and Kingdoms: 6th to 10th Centuries

section_a.title: Section A: Objective MCQs & Assertion-Reason (6 Marks)
section_a.instructions: Answer all questions. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.question_text: Which Chalukya ruler defeated Emperor Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River?
The monolithic Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora (Cave 16) was excavated top-down from a single basalt cliff under which dynasty?
What was a tax-free land or village grant given to Brahmins or scholars called during the early medieval era?
Which three dynasties were involved in the centuries-long Tripartite Struggle for control over Kannauj?

Assertion (A): Control over Kannauj became the prime objective of northern and deccan powers from the 8th to 10th centuries.
Reason (R): Kannauj symbolized imperial sovereignty after Harsha and commanded the lucrative Gangetic trade routes.
options: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_option: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for establishing economic and political motives behind the Tripartite Struggle.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): The Kudavolai system described in Uttaramerur inscriptions represented an advanced local democratic process.
Reason (R): Village committee members were chosen by drawing palm-leaf tickets from an earthen pot after verifying eligibility qualifications.
options: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_option: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for linking secret ballot mechanism with village democracy.

section_b.title: Section B: Short Answer Questions (10 Marks)
section_b.instructions: Answer all 5 questions. Each question carries 2 marks.

questions.question_text: Name the capital city of Harshavardhana and list two literary sources that document his reign.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
Capital: Kannauj (1 Mark).
Literary Sources: Harshacharita by Banabhatta, and Travelogue (Si-Yu-Ki) by Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (1 Mark).

questions.question_text: Differentiate between the Sabha and the Ur in South Indian village administration.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
Sabha: Autonomous assembly of Brahmin landholders in Brahmadeya villages (1 Mark).
Ur: General village assembly open to landholders in non-Brahmin agrarian settlements (1 Mark).

questions.question_text: Explain the role of Samantas in the early medieval feudal political structure.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Samantas were subordinate regional chieftains or landholders who provided military contingents during wars, paid annual tribute to the king, and attended imperial assemblies. When central power weakened, Samantas often declared independence (2 Marks).

questions.question_text: Which Pala king founded Vikramashila University and what was its major academic focus?
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: King Dharmapala of the Pala Dynasty founded Vikramashila University (1 Mark). Its primary academic focus was Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhist philosophy, logic, and Sanskrit grammar (1 Mark).

questions.question_text: Identify the key architectural contributions of the Pallavas at Mamallapuram.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: The Pallavas constructed monolithic rock-cut cave temples, the monolithic Pancha Rathas (Five Chariots), and the structural Shore Temple overlooking the Bay of Bengal (2 Marks).

section_c.title: Section C: Long Answer & Analytical Questions (8 Marks)
section_c.instructions: Answer both questions. Each question carries 4 marks.

questions.question_text: Analyze the Kudavolai system of election recorded in the Uttaramerur inscriptions. Detail the candidate qualifications, sub-committees, and voting mechanism.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
1. Candidate Qualifications: Ownership of taxable land, age between 35 and 70, knowledge of Vedic texts, moral integrity, and clean financial record (1 Mark).
2. Sub-Committees (Variyams): Special committees for tank irrigation, gardens, gold, taxation, and justice (1 Mark).
3. Voting Mechanism: Names of qualified candidates were written on palm-leaf tickets (kudavolai) and placed in an earthen pot (1 Mark).
4. Selection: In a full village assembly, a young boy drew tickets out of the pot to select committee members impartially (1 Mark).

questions.question_text: Describe the architectural marvel of the Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora (Cave 16) and explain why it represents an unprecedented engineering achievement.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
1. Monolithic Excavation: Carved top-down from a single volcanic basalt mountain cliff under Rashtrakuta King Krishna I (1 Mark).
2. Scale & Scale Removal: Workers excavated over 200,000 tons of solid rock without modern machinery or scaffolding (1 Mark).
3. Architectural Components: Features a multi-storeyed vimana, gateway (gopuram), courtyard, free-standing pillars, and life-sized elephant sculptures (1 Mark).
4. Artistic Mastery: Intricate relief panels depicting scenes from Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Shiva's cosmic dance (1 Mark).

section_d.title: Section D: Competency / Source-Based Case Study (6 Marks)
section_d.instructions: Read the passage carefully and answer the sub-questions that follow.
section_d.case_scenario: Passage: In the 8th century, King Krishna I issued a copper-plate charter granting a tax-free village near the Narmada River to 30 scholars. The charter, engraved in Sanskrit with the royal Rashtrakuta seal, specified that the scholars had the right to cultivate forest plots, construct irrigation tanks, and collect local market taxes. In return, the scholars established a Vedic math school (ghatika) and maintained a public manuscript repository. Local Samantas were instructed by royal decree not to interfere with the village's internal administration.

sub_questions.question_text: What type of land grant is described in this copper-plate charter? (2 Marks)
sub_questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: A Brahmadeya land grant (tax-free grant gifted to learned scholars/Brahmins) issued directly by the king (2 Marks).

sub_questions.question_text: Identify two socio-economic benefits the kingdom derived from issuing such charters. (2 Marks)
sub_questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
1. Agrarian Expansion: Bringing uncultivated forest lands under systematic farming and irrigation (1 Mark).
2. Educational & Administrative Spread: Promoting Sanskrit scholarship, literacy, and establishing royal influence in rural areas (1 Mark).

sub_questions.question_text: Why did the king explicitly instruct Samantas not to interfere in the granted village? (2 Marks)
sub_questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: To guarantee the administrative autonomy and tax-exempt status of the Brahmadeya village, preventing local feudatories from levying unauthorized taxes or usurping royal authority (2 Marks).
